title: Blockport
logline: Mine it, build it, drive it, steal it: a block-built harbor city where every lot is a fight over who owns the ground.

plot.premise: Blockport is a Tidewrights' charter town where every citizen is entitled to a lot. Someone is selling forged deeds and the Charter's original register is buried in a vault beneath the quarry. Kit Alder, a builder with a hand axe and a charter pass, can mine and build a life, drive and fight a city, or take the Ironmonger's deal and find out what the ground is really worth.

characters.name: Kit Alder
characters.role: player; newly arrived builder with a Tidewrights' charter pass

gates.hint: The Deep Works rail is dead without fuses.
The Heights lift needs a keycard or the mayor's pass.
The Foundation vault door needs the diamond-cut drill bit from Tower Three. The mayor's Foundation key shortens the drilling.
Cassian only sees people he has asked for.
Greenmeadow gates are shut at night.
Buy a deed from Odalys to build in protected lots.
Billie flies only with licensed drivers.

n1.say: Charter pass? Let me see. Kit Alder. A builder. The city needs builders; it needs fewer of everything else.

n2.say: Blockport is a Tidewrights' charter town. Every citizen gets a lot, a pickaxe and a fair chance. In practice you get a lot if you can find one. Mine yours, build it, hold it.

choices.text: What do you mean, if I can find one?

n3.say: There is an empty lot above the breakwater. Stone is in the quarry hills, wood is in the Greenmeadow; start with a hand axe, I'll lend you one. Tobi in the garage will lend you wheels if you ask nicely.

n4.say: Somebody is selling deeds to lots that were never theirs. I have six claims this month where the ink does not match the Charter seal. The Syndicate is my guess; no one will say it.

n5.say: By day. At night the hills and the meadows grow teeth. Keep a torch and a wall.

n1.say: You held your lot. That puts you ahead of half the city.

choices.text: I need to buy another deed.
Tell me about the forged deeds again.

n2.say: Five hundred bucks; honest price, honest stamp. Don't build on anything you did not buy.

n3.say: Whoever forges them has a Charter seal stamp. A real one. That means someone inside the registry or someone who took it from the Foundation vault.

n1.say: You're the new builder! I'm Tobi. That sedan in the back is my dad's, but it needs a battery, plugs and an engine block. Find me those and I'll give you the keys.

n2.say: A battery from any chest in town. Plugs from Fenn's pawn shop. The engine block, I have a lead on a wreck in Foundry Flats.

n3.say: Two-fifty and a favor. Don't scratch it.

n4.say: My dad says the best engine is a patient one.

n1.say: How's she running? Come back if you want upgrades. I know a guy with a coupe.

n2.say: Take a look.

n1.say: You're the one with the charter pass. I'll give you the speech once: Blockport is a good place that people keep trying to make into a bad one.

n2.say: If you see something, say something. If you do something, expect me to see it.

choices.text: Do you know about the forged deeds?

n3.say: I know a ledger on my desk with 40 names and no suspects. The mayor says it is a paperwork matter. I say it is a war.

n1.say: You did a job for Mire. Do not tell me you did not. I have photographs of a van, and I have a long memory.

n2.say: I will, in my own time. Right now I'd rather watch you.

n3.say: The Foundation vault, under the Deep Works. If the First Ledger exists, it's there. Mire wants it more than you do.

n1.say: The new builder. Sit. I don't offer much, so enjoy the chair.

n2.say: Blockport is not run by the mayor. It's run by whoever owns the ground. I'd like that to be me. I need a pair of hands that nobody looks at twice.

n3.say: A shipment of Charter stamps is in a van that will cross Foundry Flats at noon. Take it. Leave the driver alive if you can.

n4.say: Two thousand bucks, and a lot in Old Quarter with a view. Better, I stop being your problem.

n5.say: Then keep building. I'll buy your lot when you tire of it.

n1.say: You found the vault before I did. That was always going to happen. Let us talk about what the Ledger is worth.

n2.say: Burn it, and the city runs on my paper forever. Publish it, and everyone gets a lot and nobody has anything. Or sit beside me. I am old, builder, and tired.

choices.text: Publish the Ledger. Every plot returns to its owner.
Give me the Ledger. I'll leave the city.

n_open.say: Fool. Fine. Show me the quality of your faith.

n_leave.say: The city will be glad to see you go. I will not be.

n_truce.say: Leopold? He's been signing my paper for twenty years.

n1.say: Careful with that pick, builder! You're standing on the oldest seam in the city. The Tidewrights dug the first tunnels here before there was a harbor.

choices.text: Tell me about the Deep Works.
Can I help with the survey?

n2.say: A cavern network under the quarry hills. Rails, power, a vault. The Syndicate wants it; so does the Miners' Guild; so does the mayor, I'm told.

n3.say: Blockport crystal. Burns hot, glows, excellent for thermite. Lethal in the wrong hands. Mine it carefully.

n4.say: Mark twelve ore deposits across the hills. I'll pay you per marker.

n1.say: Charter builder? Good. I've got contracts and no hands. Forty stone and six iron, and I'll talk to you like an equal.

n2.say: Deliver to the foundry crates at Foundry Flats. Don't let the Syndicate "inspect" it.

n3.say: New seawall. And, between us, a hush-hush quarry road to the Deep Works. The Guild has a claim down there.

n1.say: You delivered. The Guild won't forget. Need ore? Need a fight? I've got both.

n2.say: Take a look.

n1.say: Fast car, quiet mouth. That's the whole résumé.

choices.text: Can you teach me to drive?

n2.say: Handbrake, countersteer, lift. Do it on the lakeshore loop; nobody cares what you dent.

n3.say: Lakeshore loop, three laps. Beat my time and I owe you a coupe.

n4.say: Whoever pays on Friday. This week it's Mire.

n1.say: Mire sold us both. I know the old rail line into the Deep Works. Get in.
Builder. Welcome to the top of the city. I hope you like the view; it's mostly paid for.

n2.say: I've been signing Mire's paper for twenty years. Charter registry fees, quarry rights, Foundry leases. The Ledger would hang me and a hundred other men.

choices.text: You can pay for my silence.
I'll take this to Inspector Calloway.

n3.say: I'll forge you a pass into the Foundation vault. After that, I never met you.

n5.say: Then I'll deny every word. Pruitt, show the builder out.

n1.say: Don't touch the model. It took six months. Oh, you're the builder? Sit, we need to talk about a vault.

n2.say: Glass Heights Tower Three. Sub-basement vault, keycard, thermite door, laser grid. I know every beam because I drew them. Cassian paid for the building; he wants what's inside.

n3.say: A drill bit that cuts the Foundation vault door. Cassian has been looking for the vault for ten years.

n4.say: Keycard from the gala. Thermite from a chem table. Then you walk in, take the bit and run before the grid resets.

n5.say: Because he owns my mortgage and my building. It's not a noble reason.

n1.say: Quiet, quiet. The rails remember footsteps.

choices.text: Show me the old rail line.

n2.say: Three fuses to light, three stations. Start at Pump Hall, then Crystal Gallery, then Foundation Station. The fuses are in my chests.

n3.say: The first Tidewrights buried their register of plots there. Every lot, every name. Whoever holds it can say who owns Blockport.

n4.say: Gus Tarn. I carried the lamp for the Tidewrights' last foreman. I'm the last one who knows where the door is.

n1.say: Everything has a price, builder. Even the things people say do not.

choices.text: Tell me about the forged deeds.

n2.say: Mm. Quality merchandise. Eighty each, and I forget your face.

n3.say: Four plugs, fifty bucks. Tobi is a good kid.

n5.say: The ink came from a blue pen. I sold one, last week, to a man in a tailored coat. That is all you are getting for free.

n1.say: Radio Blockport, on air! Hey, new face. I take requests, deliver mixtapes and gossip. In that order of importance.

n2.say: Taxi fares! Anyone who calls the station needs a ride. You drive, I pay, we both look good.

n3.say: Mire's men have been spending in Old Quarter. Someone bought a new Charter seal press. And the mayor hasn't been to the Quarter in a year.

n1.say: City folk! Seeds, hoe, and a bit of patience. The meadow forgives more than the city does.

n2.say: Till the dirt, plant seeds, water it with rain or a bucket. Three days in spring, five in autumn.

n4.say: Bring me twenty wheat for the harvest festival.

n1.say: Stray Field! Mail, medicine, mischief. The city's towers never see the roofs of the Quarry Hills like I do.

n2.say: Hop in the biplane, mind the stall. Flaps are on Q and E. The mountains are older than they look.

n3.say: Three sacks, three drop zones. Land on the road, not the church.

n1.say: Mire says be nice. I never listen.
Mr. Alder? The Mayor requests a word. At the gala tonight, if you can wear something other than overalls.

n2.say: The keycard to the Heights lift is at the front desk. Don't ask why.

n3.say: Then the Mayor will be disappointed.

entries.title: The Tidewrights' Charter
entries.text: Blockport was founded on a charter: every citizen holds a lot, the register stored in a vault no one remembers.

entries.title: Forged Deeds
entries.text: Someone with a real Charter seal stamp sells deeds to lots that already belong to others.

entries.title: The Night Mobs
entries.text: Outside the lit city, gloomers and boomlings roam after dusk. Light your lot or sleep.

entries.title: Building
entries.text: Any block can be placed. Protected lots need a deed.

entries.title: Tobi Fenwick
entries.text: A teenage mechanic with a long list of repairs and a longer list of questions.

entries.title: Driving
entries.text: Press E near a car to enter it. Police notice stolen cars.

entries.title: The Wanted Level
entries.text: Crimes add heat; witnesses add more. Cool off out of sight.

entries.title: Quarry Hills
entries.text: Mountains of ore and mobs. The Miners' Guild claims every seam.

entries.title: Old Quarter
entries.text: The oldest district: narrow streets and wide secrets.

entries.title: The Blue Ink
entries.text: The forged deeds use ink from a pen Fenn sold last week.

entries.title: Foundry Flats
entries.text: Steel, smoke and the Syndicate's home turf.

entries.title: The Syndicate
entries.text: Cassian Mire's empire of paper: forged deeds, protection and quarry leases.

entries.title: Glass Heights
entries.text: Towers built on borrowed money.

entries.title: The Gala
entries.text: The mayor's annual party; the best place to steal a keycard.

entries.title: The Mayor's Secret
entries.text: Leopold Stray has been signing Mire's paper for twenty years.

entries.title: The Foundation Vault
entries.text: The first Tidewrights' vault under the Deep Works. Needs a diamond-cut drill bit; the mayor's Foundation key shortens the drilling.

entries.title: Dex Harrow
entries.text: Mire's enforcer, loyal until he is not.

entries.title: The Deep Works
entries.text: Cavern network, rails and power long forgotten.

entries.title: Blockport Crystal
entries.text: A glowing ore that burns hot. Useful for thermite and lamps.

entries.title: The First Ledger
entries.text: The Tidewrights' register of every plot. Whoever holds it can say who owns Blockport.

entries.title: What the Ledger Says
entries.text: Every lot belonged to a citizen, not a company. Mire's deeds are fraud; the mayor's leases are fraud; the Charter was always meant to be common property.

entries.title: Foundation Station
entries.text: The terminus of the old rail. A platform nobody has stood on in sixty years.

entries.title: Radio Gossip
entries.text: Nell hears everything and broadcasts half of it.

say.text: Another ferry, another pair of hands. Welcome to Blockport.

barks.say: Radio Blockport: sunrise on the harbor. Mind the gulls.
Police scanner: units responding to a disturbance.
Breaking: citywide search under way. Drivers are advised to stay clear.
Nell: a delivery van went missing in Foundry Flats. The Syndicate denies everything, very loudly.
Mayor Stray reassures citizens that all is well. Stocks hold steady.
Dripping. Far-off rattle of an old rail.
Hold left mouse to mine; right mouse to place. E to enter a car.

endings.title: The Open Charter
endings.epilogue: Kit climbs the Foundry stacks with the First Ledger and reads it aloud over Radio Blockport. Every lot returns to the citizens; the Syndicate unravels; the mayor resigns. Odalys pins the Charter to the harbor wall. Kit builds a lighthouse.

endings.title: The Ironmonger's Seat
endings.epilogue: Kit takes the chair at Cassian's table. The city runs on a quiet ledger and a pleasant smile. The harbor lights stay on. Renna files her notes where no one will read them.

endings.title: A Quiet Foundation
endings.epilogue: Kit takes the Ledger and a boat and builds elsewhere: a small town on a coast with no charter, no deeds and no one asking. Odalys writes once a year.

endings.title: Concrete Truce
endings.epilogue: The mayor trades Mire's ledger for his own silence. The Syndicate is dissolved quietly, the forged deeds are honored with apologies, and nobody goes to trial. Blockport is better and no more honest.
